metadata.scenario: An automated robocall about extending the office's car warranty. The receptionist listens for a few seconds, realizes it's spam, and hangs up. Very short call.

transcription.text: CareFirst Home Health, this is Margaret. How can I help you today? Hi, this is George Williams. I just got a call about extending my car warranty. Oh, I see. Just to clarify, we are a home healthcare agency. Right, right—sorry about that! No problem at all! Is there anything healthcare-related I can assist you with? No, I just thought I’d check in. I had a nurse visit last week. How has everything been since then? Good, I just wish the calls would stop. I understand. Those robocalls can be really annoying! Yeah, it’s frustrating. Anyway, I might need to schedule another nursing visit soon. Sure! Would you like to speak with Robert about scheduling that? Yes, please. He was great last time! I’ll note that down. Just a moment while I check his availability. No problem! Oh, actually, it looks like he's booked today. Would you like to book for tomorrow? Tomorrow works for me! Great! I'll add you to his schedule. Thanks! And can I also ask about the medication management service? Absolutely! That service is $65 to $80 for about 30-45 minutes. Okay, I may need that, too—I'm getting confused with my meds. I can connect you with Margaret for that service if you’d like. She's our Director of Nursing. Yes, please! Alright, I’ll make sure to have her follow up with you. Thanks for your help, Margaret. I appreciate it. You're welcome, George! Have a great day. You too! Oh, and I’m hanging up now—those robocalls are really the worst! Agreed! Bye! Bye!
